purpose: Discovery audit only: identify glossary and graph gaps using open OSM snapshots plus public hiking-app cross-checks. Commercial app geometry is not ingested.

policy.commercialHikingApps: discovery/cross-check only; never copy proprietary route geometry or community prose
policy.routingGeometry: derive from OSM ways/route-relation membership and later authoritative surveys
policy.coordinates: store source geometry/element ID; point anchors must state derivation method and accuracy
policy.elevation: attach independently with source/resolution; GLO-90 is provisional, high-resolution Hessian DGM preferred
policy.benches: first-class future POIs with OSM node ID, coordinates, elevation and attributes; unknown fields remain null

publicHikingCrossChecks.notes: Community/highlight labels are discovery evidence only; canonical names/geometry require open or official corroboration.

edgeGaps.description: Named OSM hiking relations are present in source data but not modelled as route entities over the pedestrian graph. Preserve relation membership on path segments.

Merkurgraben, Schlossteichgraben, Drusel, Sichelbach, Neuer-Wasserfall-Graben and Aschgraben exist as open linear features and should form a separate hydraulic graph rather than being flattened into visitor walking edges.

OSM/Parkpflegewerk inventory lists multiple small bridges around Fontänenteich, Höllenteich, Jussow-Kaskade, Fontänenreservoir and Peneuskaskaden; each bridge should become a path-edge constraint/node where it changes crossing/access semantics.
Model the connector from each landmark/tree/bench to the pedestrian network explicitly; do not imply surface/accessibility for an unsurveyed snap.
Bench POIs should be attached to nearest path segment with side/direction and connector distance so routing can optimize rest stops.

currentRouteAuthority.warning: Older OSM Wiki route tables preserve historical K numbering; current Kassel tourism records and current OSM relation tags agree on K4=Schlosspark-Rundweg and K5=Rundweg Wasserkünste.
